axes.problem: Determine when a paper intervention's benefit transfers to a changed user context.
axes.mechanism: Construct matched one-factor perturbations around the user context and estimate zero crossings of cost-adjusted benefit.
axes.insight: A faithful unperturbed probe can hide a nearby sign reversal along a claim-linked support condition.
axes.application: Paper-derived methods and agent skills applied to user task distributions.
axes.evaluation_scope: Inside/outside/indeterminate envelope decisions and held-out benefit-sign prediction.

closest_work.title: A Unified Framework for the Transportability of Population-Level Causal Measures
closest_work.evidence: The work provides target-population causal-effect identification and estimation under covariate shift; BoundaryProbe replaces statistical transport assumptions with generated local executable perturbations.
closest_work.limitations: The candidate's local perturbation mechanism may be less rigorous than identified transport estimators.

closest_work.title: Learning about treatment effects in a new target population under transportability assumptions for relative effect measures
closest_work.evidence: The paper identifies treatment effects in a new target population under explicit transportability assumptions and directly occupies the target-context effect-transfer problem.
closest_work.limitations: No paper-to-skill artifact construction is studied.

closest_work.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
closest_work.evidence: The framework measures task- and model-specific skill utility but does not estimate context-factor zero crossings on independently supplied user distributions.
closest_work.limitations: It already defeats broad novelty claims about task-specific skill utility.

closest_work.title: How NOT to benchmark your SITE metric: Beyond Static Leaderboards and Towards Realistic Evaluation
closest_work.evidence: It shows static model spaces and performance hierarchies inflate transferability metrics, threatening a small fixed-row applicability benchmark.
closest_work.limitations: It does not construct claim-conditioned task perturbations.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
One-factor envelopes do not identify interactions, and eight rows cannot validate broad transport claims.
